# @adhd/stealth-core-browser

> Node.js library that launches and reads a local Chrome over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Chrome is started without --enable-automation and pages are read without Runtime.evaluate. Library only; the CLI and MCP server are in @adhd/stealth-search.

Requires Node.js >= 22.5. Single entry (package root), no subpath exports. Version 0.x: the six verbs are the stable surface, namespaces are experimental until 1.0. Verified on macOS; Linux and Windows are untested.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): overview, install, quickstart
- [Verbs](docs/VERBS.md): input, return shape and errors of each verb
- [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md): every default (host 127.0.0.1, port 9222, profile Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome-CDP, state directory), options, platform support
- [Responsible use](docs/RESPONSIBLE-USE.md): what "stealth" means (two choices), terms of service, robots.txt, rate limits, read-only profile access
- [Examples](docs/EXAMPLES.md): every runnable file under examples/ with its scenario
- [Errors](docs/ERRORS.md): StealthCoreBrowserError code registry with exit codes and remediation
- [Reference](docs/reference/README.md): namespace reference (cdp, storage, capture, parsers, chromeManager)
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)
- [Agent notes](AGENTS.md)

## API

- Verbs: chromeStatus, launchChrome, shutdownChrome, listPageTargets, checkChromeActivity, getPageContext
- Namespaces: cdp, storage, capture, parsers, chromeManager, lifecycle, recording, endpoint
- Errors: StealthCoreBrowserError, ERROR_CODES, exitCodeFor

## Limits

- Host is loopback-only unless the hosting process calls endpoint.configureEndpointPolicy.
- Google result-page parsers are provisional (synthetic-fixture verified).
- Do not connect to port 9222 in tests; examples use port 9333.
